items.title: v2.1.292
items.bullet_md:

  - The Agent tool gains an effort parameter for sub-agent reasoning level

items.title: ReviewBench: An open benchmark for AI code review
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[ReviewBench: An open benchmark for AI code review](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/reviewbench-an-open-benchmark-for-ai-code-review/)** — _GitHub AI blog_. — GitHub launched ReviewBench to score AI code-review agents on 219 real pull requests.
  - 219 PRs from 187 open-source repos across 19 languages
  - Multi-source golden set: human reviewers, frontier LLMs, static analysis
  - Senior engineers agreed with its labels 96.6% of the time
  - Reports grounded and augmented precision/recall, sliced by severity

score_components.taste_reason: GitHub's own open benchmark for AI code-review agents with representative PRs and production-aligned metrics — concrete new eval infrastructure from a credible source, not yet in state-of-ai.

items.title: Remote control for local agents
items.bullet_md:
- 🛠 **[Remote control for local agents](https://cursor.com/changelog/remote-control-local-agents)** — _Cursor changelog_. — Cursor's iOS app can now view and reply to local agents running on your computer.
  - Remote Control is on by default, except for Enterprise organizations
  - Pair by tapping a computer, then approving in the desktop app
  - Agents keep running locally; the computer must stay on and online
  - A desktop setting can keep the computer awake while you're away

score_components.taste_reason: Genuinely new workflow — remote-monitoring local agents from iOS — but thin on how it works or any limits.

items.title: v1.0.4

items.title: Grep or Embeddings? Agentic Search Over Company Documents — George He, LlamaIndex
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Grep or Embeddings? Agentic Search Over Company Documents — George He, LlamaIndex](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X4w2Pkz5tDY) — **AI Engineer** (23m22s). — When to give agents pre-indexed search versus plain file traversal, for company documents rather than code. - Code is small, text-based, local, so Claude Code skipped embeddings - Company files are huge, messy, multimodal and permissioned - LlamaParse and open-source LiteParse parse complex PDFs and tables - Demo builds a cash-flow table from 135 Alphabet filings

score_components.taste_reason: Credible AI Engineer talk from a LlamaIndex lead giving practitioner reasoning on when agents need indexed retrieval vs plain grep — a real design decision, not hype.

items.title: Paperclip: Run a Small AI Agent Team (Claude Code + Codex) Without the Chaos
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Paperclip: Run a Small AI Agent Team (Claude Code + Codex) Without the Chaos](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RknGPBeA6AQ) — **AICodeKing** (10m48s). — How to run a small team of coding agents with Paperclip, a free MIT-licensed control plane. - Adapters connect Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode and Pi - Setup needs Node 24.11+ and one command; it bundles PostgreSQL - Review stages, strategy approvals and budgets are all enforced - Best if you already coordinate several agents; overkill for one

score_components.taste_reason: Concrete open-source coordinator for multi-harness agent teams (Claude Code + Codex + Gemini CLI via adapters) — genuinely useful pattern for a daily-harness reader, if a fairly standard demo.

items.title: Build Your First MCP Server in Python: 20 Lines, Real Tools
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Build Your First MCP Server in Python: 20 Lines, Real Tools](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RGryq0Zt9og) — **Soumya** (5m58s). — A six-minute walkthrough builds a working MCP server in about 20 lines of Python and wires it into Claude. - Type hints become the tool schema; the docstring becomes its description - Raising ToolError returns fix-it advice to the model instead of failing - Never print in a stdio server — it breaks the protocol - Test with MCP Inspector, then connect Claude Desktop and Claude Code

score_components.taste_reason: Beginner MCP-server tutorial — useful for a newcomer but nothing a daily Claude Code user doesn't already know, no novel pattern or numbers.

items.title: Tecent Octop (Opensource): Wait, Tencent just ENDED OpenAI Dots & Muse!?
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Tecent Octop (Opensource): Wait, Tencent just ENDED OpenAI Dots & Muse!?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fw1b7Lz5TE4) — **AICodeKing** (12m44s). — Tencent's Octop is a free, MIT-licensed, self-hosted AI assistant that unites experts, documents and scheduled tasks. - Experts each get their own workspace, model and prompt files - Knowledge bases use local ONNX embeddings so answers cite your documents - An expert can hand file writing to OpenCode over ACP - The app is free but you supply the model; Ollama is supported

score_components.taste_reason: Clickbait title ('just ENDED OpenAI') from a low-credibility channel, and the body only says a free open-source terminal assistant exists — no benchmark or comparison to back the framing.

items.title: Claude Code + /prove-it-better = AI That PROVES It's Better (FREE Skill)
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Claude Code + /prove-it-better = AI That PROVES It's Better (FREE Skill)](https://youtube.com/watch?v=hNLHEC-4okw) — **Income stream surfers** (7m41s). — A free Claude Code skill, /prove-it-better, for anyone who wants changes to prove they actually improved things instead of trusting a confident claim: it researches the problem and the real data first, then runs old versus new on the same real inputs through a blind A/B judge — outputs labelled A and B, judged twice with the order swapped, and both verdicts must agree — shipping only the winners. The author ran it about 9 hours overnight rebuilding his AI SEO tool Harbor, and it later found 5 unnecessary Convex seats, saving $75 a month.

score_components.taste_reason: Concrete Claude Code skill with a real method (blind A/B, order-swapped double verdict) and a saving ($75/mo), though the 'AI That PROVES It's Better' title is clickbaity.
